Nestled on the left bank of the Red River, Bat Trang Market, also known as Chợ Bát Tràng, is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Vietnam. This ancient pottery market, situated approximately ten kilometers from the heart of Hanoi, has been a hub of artisanal craftsmanship for centuries.

This ancient pottery market, situated approximately ten kilometers from the heart of Hanoi, has been a hub of artisanal craftsmanship for centuries. According to legend, pottery-making families from the Bo Bat region, who had mastered the art of firing clay into jade glaze, settled in this area during the Ly Dynasty, combining their ancestral name with the name of their new home to form "Bat Trang" – the place where the famous jade-glazed pottery was born.

As one approaches the market, the rustic charm of the red-bricked village roads, low, old houses, and riverside trees creates a sense of nostalgia, transporting visitors to a bygone era. The market's architecture, comprising a large, domed structure made of brick and concrete, is a marvel of traditional Vietnamese craftsmanship.
